transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, uh… I guess what brings me in is I can’t stop jumping out of my skin. Like at work, if a breaker snaps or a tool hits the floor, I’m already halfway turned around before I even know what happened. Or if somebody walks up behind me—man, I hate that. My heart just starts pounding, and it keeps going long after everyone else is laughing it off or getting back to work.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I do maintenance, so loud stuff happens all the time, you know? Breakers, ladders, carts, all that. But it’s like my body doesn’t know the difference anymore.

Do you find yourself especially anxious or fearful when you're around other people, especially in situations where you feel like you're being watched or might be judged, like when you're working in front of others?

I don’t know if it’s that exactly… like being judged? I mean, nobody likes having the boss standing there watching you fix something, right? Makes your hands feel stupid.

But I can’t really say it’s about people judging me. Sometimes it’s just… I’m trying to do the job, and there’s noise, guys walking around, somebody talking too close, and I lose track of what I was doing. Like yesterday I was looking for a washer, the little flat kind, and I swear the whole drawer was full of everything except what I needed—screws, anchors, old junk somebody should’ve thrown out months ago. That place is a mess.

So, uh… around people, yeah, I can get on edge, but I don’t know if it’s because I think they’re watching me. I haven’t really thought of it like that.
Do you often feel on high alert or worried about things happening around you, even when you're not at work or around other people?

Uh… I’m not sure. I mean, I notice stuff when I’m out, sure, but I don’t know if I’d call it high alert all the time.

Like, if I’m at the store, I’m mostly just trying to get in and out because the lines are always backed up and they move everything around—last week I couldn’t find the damn air filters because they changed the aisle layout again. But… worried about things happening around me? I don’t know. Maybe sometimes, but I haven’t really thought about it that way.
Outside of work and other loud environments, do you ever find yourself getting startled very easily, like by a sudden sound or someone approaching you when you didn’t expect it?

Yeah… yeah, not just at work. I mean, work is where it happens the most because there’s always something banging or snapping or somebody dropping a tool, but even outside of that, if something sudden happens, I jump hard.

Like if someone comes up behind me and I didn’t hear them, my whole body reacts before I can think. Heart starts hammering, and then it doesn’t just settle right away. Everybody else is already past it, you know, like “what’s your problem?” and I’m still standing there trying to get myself back down.

It’s stupid stuff too, like a door shutting too hard or something falling in the other room… and then I’m irritated because I know it shouldn’t be that big of a deal. But my body acts like it is.
Do you ever feel like your body is always on edge, like you're waiting for something to happen, even when there's no real danger around?

I don’t know… “always” is a big word. I mean, my body gets tense, sure, but sometimes it’s just because I’ve been crawling under a sink or hauling stuff and my back’s all locked up, you know?

Waiting for something to happen… I’m not sure how to answer that. Like, if I’m at home and the fridge kicks on, I notice it, but then again that fridge makes this whining sound it’s been making forever, and I keep telling myself I’m gonna pull it out and check the coils but then there’s always something else.

So… maybe? I don’t know if it’s no real danger or just me being wound up. I haven’t really sorted it out like that.
Do you ever notice that you’re extra sensitive to things happening around you even during quiet or calm times, like when you’re sitting alone at home watching TV or trying to relax?

Yeah… I guess I do. Even when it’s quiet, I’m still catching every little sound more than I should.

But the big thing—the thing that actually got me in here—is I can’t stop jumping out of my skin. Like a breaker snaps, or a tool drops, or somebody comes up behind me and I didn’t know they were there… I mean, I know that’s not exactly sitting on the couch, but it’s the same kind of thing. My heart just takes off, and it keeps hammering after everybody else is already done reacting.

And then I’m standing there mad at myself, because it’s just a noise. Like, I should be able to shake it off, but my body doesn’t get the memo.
Do you ever feel like you’re constantly scanning your surroundings, even when there’s no immediate threat or reason to be on edge?

I’m not sure I’d call it scanning, exactly. I mean, I look around, but doesn’t everybody? Like if I’m in a room I’ll notice where people are, or if someone’s moving around behind me, but I don’t know if that’s me being on edge or just… paying attention.

Sometimes I think maybe I’m just used to checking things because of work. You’re always looking for where the ladder is, where the cords are, if somebody left something in the way—one time a guy left a fitting right in the walkway and I almost rolled my ankle, so now I catch myself looking down all the time. But that’s not really danger, I guess, that’s just not wanting to trip over somebody’s mess.

So… yeah, I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed myself doing it like that, like consciously searching for threats or anything. It’s more just… I’m aware of stuff, maybe too much sometimes, but I can’t say for sure.

Even in completely safe and familiar places, like your bedroom at night or sitting in your car, do you ever feel like your body still reacts strongly to small, normal things—like a clock ticking, a breeze moving something, or your own shadow?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know about a clock ticking exactly. I’ve got one of those digital ones now because the old one drove me nuts, but that might’ve just been the cheap plastic gears or whatever.

But the small normal stuff, yeah. What got me to finally come in is I keep jumping like something bad just happened. A breaker snaps at work, or somebody drops a tool, or someone walks up behind me and says something before I know they’re there… and I just about come out of my skin.

And then my heart’s going hard, like way after everyone else has already laughed it off or gone back to what they were doing. I’ll be standing there trying to act normal, but my body’s still reacting like it didn’t get the message that it was nothing.
Have you noticed that these strong reactions to sounds or surprises have been happening more often or feel more intense since a specific event or experience you went through?

Yeah… I mean, that’s kind of the part I keep circling back to. I don’t know if I’ve got a clean before-and-after lined up in my head, like “this day it started,” you know?

But what brought me in is I can’t stop jumping out of my skin now. A breaker snaps, or a tool drops, or somebody comes up behind me and I didn’t hear them, and it’s like my whole body fires off before I can even think. And then everybody else just keeps moving, like it was nothing, and I’m still standing there with my heart hammering.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I’ll try to play it off, maybe say something about needing another coffee or whatever, but inside I’m still rattled. Like the noise is over, but my body’s acting like it isn’t.
Have you ever experienced or witnessed a serious accident, injury, or other traumatic event that has stayed with you, even if it happened a while ago?

Yeah… there was something. I don’t always like getting into it because then it’s like my head starts pulling pieces of it back up whether I want it to or not.

It was an accident at work, and there was a trainee there. I’ll be doing something normal now, like loading tools in the truck, checking straps, whatever, and out of nowhere I’ll see that flash in my head or hear him yelling. It’s not like I’m sitting there trying to remember it. It just hits me, and for a second it feels like I’m right back there again.

And then I’ll lose track of what I was even doing. Like I’ll be holding a ratchet or counting fittings and suddenly I’m somewhere else in my head. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but it just… knocks me sideways.
